title: velocity_spike entries have negative 30-day alpha — do not trade them long
detail: After removing split-contaminated outcomes and deduplicating, velocity_spike shows a 30-day median of -7.50% against SPY's +0.23% over the same window: -7.73pp of alpha across n=43. The 5-day median is mildly positive (+4.06% vs SPY +1.73%), so the signal front-runs nothing and mean-reverts hard. Mechanism: every 'combined' signal on 2026-08-21 fired on a name that had ALREADY moved 3-15% that same session (HOOD +13.7%, SLS +15.4%, MSTR +6.1%). Entry is after the move is complete. If this trigger is kept, test it as a fade or short, not a long.
evidence: Corrected edge table, docs/2026-08-29_signal_validation_learnings.md §3. n=43 deduped, split-guarded.

title: Roll-up/component reconciliation does not work — use grain separation instead
detail: Attempted to reconcile OpenInsider cluster roll-up rows against the individual Form 4 rows they summarise. Only 4 of 352 roll-ups reconcile exactly; 343 are unexplainable. Root cause: the individual views (collect_ceo_cfo_buys, collect_insider_purchases) only scrape officers above a dollar floor, so the roll-up's other buyers were never collected and there is no complete component set to reconcile against. Do not re-attempt this. The working approach is grain SEPARATION — totals come from exactly one grain, never a cross-grain sum.
evidence: Measured across the full insiders table 2026-08-23. See src/analysis/insider_grain.py module docstring.

title: The +20%/-10% bracket is EV-neutral and mis-calibrated for low-volatility names
detail: Gambler's ruin on a driftless asset: P(take-profit first) = 10/(10+20) = 33.3%, so EV = (1/3)(+20%) + (2/3)(-10%) = 0.00% before costs. The bracket contributes nothing; all expectancy must come from the signal. Worse, it was tuned on high-vol momentum names. On a 20%-annualised-vol instrument the -10% stop is 8.1 sigma away (14% chance of touch in 30d) and the +20% target is 16.2 sigma away (0.3% chance) — the take-profit is decoration. Express barriers in multiples of realised daily sigma, with a floor at the nearest structural level, not as fixed percentages.
evidence: First-passage probabilities computed from 20-day realised vol; verified against REFI (19.7% ann., 1.24%/day).

title: SQLite cannot be written over the device mount — work in the container and commit the file
detail: Writing to data/sentiment.db through the mounted device folder fails with 'sqlite3.OperationalError: disk I/O error' at commit and leaves a stale rollback journal behind, which device_bash cannot delete. The transaction rolls back cleanly (integrity_check ok) but nothing is written. Correct workflow: stage the DB into the container, do all SQLite work there, commit the finished file back via device_commit_files. Verify by sha256 on both sides.
evidence: Reproduced 2026-08-23 running utils/repair_outcomes_and_dupes.py --apply over the mount.

title: yfinance transport is blocked in the cloud container — use plain-TLS urllib for bars
detail: yfinance 1.6.0 drives HTTP through curl_cffi with browser TLS impersonation. The container's egress proxy resets every such connection ('curl: (35) Recv failure: Connection reset by peer') — the collector scored 0/452 tickers. Plain-TLS urllib to the identical Yahoo chart endpoint (query1.finance.yahoo.com/v8/finance/chart/SYMBOL) works normally. Workaround: a transport-only shim exposing collect_historical_prices(), driven by the project's own backfill_price_bars() so the gap logic and write path are unchanged. This is a CONTAINER-ONLY issue; yfinance works fine in the Windows venv.
evidence: 0/452 via yfinance vs 446/452 via urllib shim, same session, 2026-08-23. Spot-checked against Robinhood: CC $15.97, KEEL $3.32, INTC $90.07 all exact.

title: Split contamination in outcomes.py fabricated forward returns up to +707%
detail: src/analysis/outcomes.py used price_at_signal (captured live, unadjusted) as the baseline against price_bars closes (retroactively split-adjusted). Mixing adjustment bases fabricates returns: SOXS 2026-05-22 recorded +706.78% at 5d, SPCX +593.24%. Those two rows alone lifted velocity_spike's 5-day mean from +5.33% to +34.76% while barely moving the median — the signature of outlier contamination. Fixed in v1.1.0: baseline is always the signal-day bar close, plus a _split_boundary() guard that leaves an outcome NULL rather than writing a number across a >2x or <0.5x single-session discontinuity.
evidence: SOXS bars: $1,146.15 close on 05-22 -> $62.18 on 05-26, volume 1.88M -> 40.4M. price_at_signal was $7.67.

title: insiders table was 78% duplicate rows, inflating every cluster count
detail: No UNIQUE constraint and a plain INSERT. OpenInsider's cluster / CEO-CFO / purchase views overlap, so each trade landed several times per run and again on every later run: 3,400 rows -> 753 distinct. Because the cluster trigger counts rows, one CEO purchase read as a seven-buyer cluster — Intel's '7 insiders bought $69,999,895' was a single $10.0M purchase counted seven times. Fixed with INSERT OR IGNORE plus a unique index on the Form 4 natural key.
evidence: Verified live: a later collector run offered 204 rows and stored 4. Under the old code all 204 would have inserted.

title: Roll-up rows were counted alongside the Form 4 rows they summarise (47% of the table)
detail: OpenInsider's cluster view returns aggregate rows summing several Form 4 filings; 352 of 753 rows are roll-ups. They sat in the same table as their own components and the trigger counted both. Fixed with src/analysis/insider_grain.py: explicit row_grain, totals drawn from exactly one grain (named in verdict.basis), cluster status established by EITHER >=2 distinct named Form 4 buyers OR the presence of a roll-up.
evidence: KEEL 2026-08-20 roll-up of 116,129 sh = CEO 58,888 + COO 26,472 + COO 30,769, confirmed against SEC filings.

title: Offering participation and exercises-at-strike were read as open-market conviction
detail: Form 4 code 'P' covers open-market buys, registered-offering participation and exercises at strike alike, and the collector flattened OpenInsider's qualified string ('P - Purchase+OE') to bare 'P' before storage. Intel's CEO bought 105,263 shares at exactly $95.00 INSIDE a $20B upsized offering (210.5M new shares) and the pipeline scored it as a $10M conviction buy. Fixed: preserve acquisition_code; derive acquisition_channel from a bar-range test — an open-market fill must print inside that session's low-high range. Below the low = off-market (offerings price at a discount); above the high = data anomaly, labelled separately.
evidence: INTC $95.00 vs 95.35-98.35 session range. MSTR $99.62 vs 132.76-139.78. Zero false positives against KEEL/CC/OPEN open-market buys. After widening bar coverage to 396/405 form4 rows: 15.6% of all Form 4 'purchases' were not open-market priced.

title: The insider_cluster edge was manufactured by the duplicate rows — sample collapsed 6 to 2
detail: Re-running the historical insider_cluster signals through grain and channel filtering drops four of six, and EVERY large winner is among them: AMC +26.49% (one buy, counted twice), SOFI +17.38% and +13.51% (three buys, all Anthony Noto), CIA +2.35% (four buys, all Jon Stenberg). The two survivors — GO and NKE — are the only ones with genuine multi-insider cluster filings, and their 30-day median is +1.83% against SPY's +0.23%. Verified this is not retrospective data loss: every dropped ticker still has all its rows; they are one person's repeat buying that row-counting read as a cluster.
evidence: docs/2026-08-29_signal_validation_learnings.md §3.

title: Sample independence is the binding constraint — 45 of 54 outcomes share one date
detail: The edge table looks like n=54 but 45 outcomes come from a single observation date (2026-05-22) and there are only 4 distinct dates in total. Cross-sectionally correlated observations are not independent samples; effective n is closer to 4. No per-trigger conclusion drawn from this table should be treated as significant. At one pipeline run per weekday, a usable sample is months away. This is the single strongest argument for staying on paper.
evidence: SELECT date(created_at), COUNT(*) FROM signals WHERE outcome_pct IS NOT NULL GROUP BY 1.

title: Insider clusters cannot signal without Reddit chatter — 44 live clusters were invisible
detail: generate_signals() iterates velocity_data.keys(), so a qualifying insider cluster on a ticker nobody posts about can never produce a signal. On 2026-08-24 there were 44 live qualifying clusters and almost none could signal; CC had a genuine cluster and produced nothing for exactly this reason. This structurally subordinates the only non-negative trigger to social mentions. Proposed fix: iterate the union of velocity tickers and tickers with live clusters.
evidence: Observed during the 2026-08-24 signal generation run. 33 signals produced, 29 of them velocity_spike.

title: The Robinhood MCP has no OCO — one exit order claims all the shares
detail: There is no bracket/OCO order type in the tool surface. A protective stop and a take-profit limit cannot coexist on the same shares: whichever is placed first sets shares_held_for_sells to the full quantity and shares_available_for_sells to 0. Any change to the exit plan must begin with cancelling the existing order. Consequence: the paper engine's +20/-10 bracket cannot be reproduced live, and live results will diverge from backtest on exit behaviour alone.
evidence: Observed directly on the REFI position: 18 shares held_for_sells with the stop open, 18 available after cancelling.

title: Bar coverage gates the acquisition-channel test
detail: The channel test needs a price bar for the trade date. With only signal+trade tickers in the spine it reached 23 of 401 Form 4 rows (5.7%). Widening the bar-backfill universe to include insider tickers (160 -> 452) raised coverage to 396 of 405 and exposed 63 contaminated rows instead of 4. Rows without a bar stay 'unverified' and cannot be checked — BABA's apparent $15.3M cluster was priced at $14.24 against a ~$119 ADR (that is the Hong Kong listing) and was caught by eye, not by the classifier.
evidence: get_signal_and_trade_tickers() now unions the insiders table; docstring records the 23/401 measurement.

title: Ran one live $200 execution test (REFI) to validate the order path end to end
detail: Selected REFI as the only candidate clearing all four filters: two named open-market Form 4 buyers (both Co-CEOs), corroborated by a company press release (~54,000 sh / ~$673,000 by officers and directors), the lowest stop-out probability in the candidate set (14% vs 76-85% for the high-volatility names), and no earnings inside the window. Entry 18 sh @ $10.85 on 2026-08-25, $195.30. The purpose was to prove the execution path, not to express a view — there was no measured edge behind it and that was stated at the time.
evidence: Order 6a8cd230-bf1c-498a-a40c-43c205b0f3e3, filled 09:30:00 ET, zero fees.

title: The execution path works: signal to fill to automated stop to exit, fully auditable
detail: Validated end to end: grain-verified cluster -> review_equity_order -> place_equity_order -> fill -> scheduled task read the ACTUAL fill price and derived the stop from it (not the estimate) -> stop revised on new analysis -> exit placed. Every step is recoverable from order ids and placed_agent='agentic' filtering. This half of the system is trustworthy. One unexplained detail: the scheduled task's stop was created ~10.5 hours after its trigger time; outcome was correct, cause unknown.

title: A dividend is not added return over a short window — the ex-date drop offsets it
detail: Initially framed REFI's 17.6% yield as '+4.3% per quarter' on the position. That is wrong. On the ex-date you receive the cash AND the share price drops by approximately the same amount; net effect that day is zero. A high yield is only real return if the price holds up across quarters. Correcting this materially weakened the REFI case after the position was already open — the yield was found after selection, not before it. Lesson: pull dividend and credit profile BEFORE selecting, not after.
evidence: $0.47/sh on 18 sh = $8.46 cash; simultaneous price drop 18 x $0.47 = $8.46.

title: Stop placement should be set against structural levels, not round percentages
detail: A -10% stop on REFI landed at $9.77 — eight cents above the 52-week low of $9.69, a level tested four weeks earlier. Widening to $9.55 (below the low) LOWERED expected loss despite raising the loss-if-hit, because it removed the probability of being knocked out by an ordinary retest: 20.5% x -$19.44 = -$3.99 versus 11.6% x -$23.40 = -$2.72. Also account for the ex-dividend drop: a $0.47 dividend on a $10.69 stock mechanically moves price 4.4% toward the stop, and the stop cannot tell that is not a loss.
evidence: First-passage probabilities over 30 trading days at 1.24% daily sigma.

title: Closed the REFI position and reverted to paper-only until a real sample exists
detail: Exited at roughly -$3 on $195.30. Reasoning: the pipeline half of the experiment succeeded and is proven, the signal half has no measured edge, and with zero edge the expected value of holding is approximately zero minus costs (simulated 60 trading days, zero drift: mean -$2.08, 39% chance of profit, 5th/95th percentile -$14.94/+$28.19). Keeping capital tied up to keep testing already-proven plumbing was not worth it. Reverse this decision when a trigger shows measured edge across independent observation dates.

title: acquisition_code cannot be backfilled for historical rows
detail: The collector flattened OpenInsider's qualified trade-type string to bare 'P' and discarded the original before it ever reached the database. Only rows collected after 2026-08-23 carry a code. Historical rows are classified on the bar-range test alone, which cannot detect a same-day offering priced inside the session range.
evidence: src/collectors/openinsider.py line ~257 before the fix.

title: min_insiders=2 cannot distinguish a two-person cluster from a twenty-person one
detail: With roll-ups acting as an alternate route to cluster status, a genuine broad cluster and a bare two-buyer cluster produce identical verdicts. Roll-up rows carry no buyer count (the scraper blanks insider_name/title for them), so the information needed to grade cluster breadth is not collected. Worth investigating whether OpenInsider's cluster view exposes a count column that could be captured.
evidence: 401 of 753 rows carry a name; all 352 roll-ups do not.

title: paper_trades.pnl is a dead column — annotated, not migrated
detail: pnl is never written and never read; every code path and dashboard uses profit_loss, which is fully populated. An earlier session flagged the NULLs as a defect; that was a mis-read of the schema. Left in place per the historical-preservation rule rather than migrated, since removing it has blast radius and no benefit.
evidence: grep for pnl/profit_loss across src/; 22/22 closed trades have profit_loss, 0 have pnl.
